Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a person who solved a problem in a smart way

描述一个用聪明方式解决问题的人

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a person who solved a problem in a smart way

  • Who this person is (这个人是谁)
  • What the problem was (问题是什么)
  • How he/she solved it (他/她如何解决)
  • And explain why you think he/she did it in a smart way (并解释为什么你觉得他/她的方式很聪明)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a person who solved a problem in a smart way

I'd like to talk about my cousin, who solved a computer problem for me in a way that still amazes me. He's a few years older than me, and he's always been the person in the family who fixes things. First of all, who he is: he's my cousin, and he's really good with his hands. He repairs routers and computers at home, so when something breaks, everyone calls him. The problem happened about a year ago, when my computer suddenly wouldn't turn on. I was in a panic, because I had an assignment due the next day, and I had no idea what was wrong. I was already imagining having to take it to a repair shop and paying a lot of money. How he solved it was the impressive part. He came over, looked at the computer for about two minutes, and then calmly opened the case. He found that the memory stick was loose, so he simply took it out and pushed it back in firmly. The computer started up right away, and the whole thing took him less than five minutes. The reason I think it was smart is that he didn't panic or try random fixes. He knew where to look, because he understood how the machine works, and he solved the problem at the root instead of guessing. Looking back, I realised that being smart isn't just about knowledge, it's about staying calm and thinking clearly when everyone else is panicking.

讲的是表哥，动手能力强，家里路由器、电脑坏了都找他修。一年前我电脑突然开不了机，第二天要交作业，急得不行，都想着要送修花钱了。他来了看了两分钟，冷静打开机箱，发现内存条松了，拔出来重新插紧，电脑马上就好了，全程不到五分钟。觉得他聪明是因为他不慌不乱、不瞎试，懂机器原理所以知道该看哪里，从根源解决问题。聪明不只是知识，更是别人慌乱时保持冷静、想清楚。

Q2Do you think children are born smart or they learn to become smart?

I think it's a combination of both. Some children are born with natural advantages, like quick thinking or a good memory, which gives them a head start. However, intelligence is mostly developed through learning and experience. A child who reads, asks questions and practises will become smarter over time, regardless of their starting point. So I'd say everyone is born with potential, but it's the learning that turns that potential into real ability.

两者结合。有些孩子天生有优势，比如反应快、记性好，起点更高；但智力主要靠学习和经验发展。爱读书、爱提问、勤练习的孩子会越来越聪明，不管起点如何。人人天生有潜力，是学习把潜力变成真正的能力。

Q3How do children become smart at school?

Children become smart at school mainly through good habits and curiosity. Asking questions is a big part of it, because it shows they're thinking deeply rather than just memorising. Practising regularly also matters, since skills like maths and writing improve with repetition. On top of that, learning from mistakes helps them grow, because smart children treat errors as chances to improve. So I'd say it's a mix of curiosity, practice and the right attitude.

孩子在学校变聪明主要靠好习惯和好奇心。提问很重要，说明他们在深入思考而不是死记硬背；定期练习也关键，数学写作这类技能靠重复提高；还要从错误中学习，聪明的孩子把错误当改进的机会。是好奇心、练习和正确态度的结合。

Q4Why are some people well-rounded and others only good at one thing?

I think it comes down to interests, opportunities and personality. People who are curious about many things and have the chance to try different activities tend to become well-rounded. Others may find one thing they love early on and pour all their time into it, which naturally makes them specialists. There's nothing wrong with either path, since society needs both generalists and specialists. So it's largely about how people choose to spend their time and energy.

取决于兴趣、机会和性格。对很多事好奇、有机会尝试不同活动的人往往全面发展；另一些人很早就找到热爱的一件事，把所有时间投入进去，自然成为专家。两条路都没错，社会既需要通才也需要专才。主要看人怎么分配时间和精力。

Q5Why does modern society need talents of all kinds?

Modern society is so complex that no single type of talent can solve all its problems. We need engineers to build technology, doctors to keep people healthy, artists to enrich culture and teachers to pass on knowledge. Each field depends on the others, so a society with only one kind of talent would quickly fall apart. In that sense, diversity of talent is what keeps society balanced and moving forward.

现代社会太复杂，单一类型的人才解决不了所有问题。需要工程师造技术、医生保健康、艺术家丰富文化、教师传承知识。每个领域都依赖其他领域，只有一种人才的社会很快就会崩溃。人才多样性让社会保持平衡、向前发展。

Q6Do you think smart children are happier than other children?

I don't think smart children are automatically happier. Intelligence can bring advantages, like doing well at school and solving problems easily, but it can also bring pressure, since people expect more from them. Happiness depends more on things like family support, friendships and whether they can pursue what they love. A smart child under too much pressure might actually be less happy than an average child with a relaxed life. So intelligence and happiness aren't directly connected.

聪明的孩子不一定更快乐。智力带来优势，比如学习好、解决问题轻松，但也带来压力，因为别人对他们期望更高。快乐更取决于家庭支持、友谊和能否追求所爱。压力过大的聪明孩子可能还不如生活轻松的普通孩子快乐。智力和快乐没有直接关系。

Q7Is it important for schools to identify and develop each student's talents?

Yes, I think it's important, because every student has strengths that might not show up in regular exams. If schools can identify these talents early, they can help students develop them, which builds confidence and motivation. That said, schools should be careful not to label children or push them too hard in one direction. The goal should be to support each student's potential while keeping a broad education, rather than forcing everyone into the same mould.

重要，因为每个学生都有常规考试看不出的长处。学校早点发现这些才能并帮助发展，能建立自信和动力。但学校要小心不要给孩子贴标签或往一个方向逼太狠。目标应该是支持每个学生的潜力，同时保持全面教育，而不是把所有人塞进同一个模子。
